summary: This bill establishes a program to provide monthly payments to eligible pregnant women and caregivers of eligible children, while simultaneously repealing the existing child tax credit.

scores.thoughts: This bill establishes a new program for monthly payments to pregnant women and caregivers of eligible children, explicitly stating that "such sums as are necessary to carry out this section" are appropriated from the Treasury. This directly increases government spending.

The bill repeals the existing Child Tax Credit (Section 24 of the Internal Revenue Code) and makes conforming amendments. While it replaces it with a direct payment program, the repeal of a tax credit effectively removes a tax reduction mechanism, which could be seen as increasing the tax burden for some, or at least eliminating a tax benefit.

By creating a new program for direct monthly payments with an open-ended appropriation and simultaneously repealing a tax credit, the bill is likely to increase the national debt through increased outlays and potentially reduced revenue (depending on the net effect of the CTC repeal vs. new spending).

The bill creates a new open-ended entitlement program with mandatory monthly payments to pregnant women and caregivers, funded by an unlimited appropriation of 'such sums as are necessary' from the Treasury. While it repeals the Child Tax Credit, the legislation's core purpose is expanding direct family support spending rather than achieving net deficit reduction, so it leans toward accepting larger deficits to fund priorities.
